name: Should chinking be done before or after interior log staining?

mainEntity.name: Should chinking be done before or after interior log staining?

acceptedAnswer.text: The proper sequence depends on whether you are replacing existing chinking or working with stable materials. If existing chinking or caulking is intact and accepts stain, it can remain in place, though many owners prefer staining logs first so lines remain sharp. When applying fresh chinking, professionals typically clean, prep, and apply the stain coat to the logs first. Once the stain dries fully, backing rods and chinking material are applied into the joints. This prevents stain drips from discoloring fresh chinking lines. Finally, a clear coat can be applied over the logs to protect the overall finish.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stain is typically applied to the logs before installing new chinking. This avoids stain splatters on fresh chink lines and keeps the borders neat and clean.
